# Sway bar links and bushings

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Clean spindles with a stiff wire brush using quick back-and-forth vibrating motions. [t811]

[Partial] Spray PB Blaster on bolts and jack up the truck at preferred points using h-frame rails. [t856]

[Partial] Undo the bottom spindle bolt, loosen its nut, drive it out with a hammer and random grade eight bolts using PB Blaster. [t856]

[Partial] Remove the CV axle from the differential and use a two-jawed seal puller. [t754]

[Partial] Install four Febest Camber Bolts and Nissan Cam Washers on the vehicle's lower control arms. [t642]

Drill out stock bushings, saw through outer sleeves, then install Delrin LCA Bushings with copper anti-seize. [t270]

Grease the outside of the Delrin LCA bushing sleeves with a good quality synthetic grease. [t270]

[Partial] Remove the front UCA bolt, then pull and twist the rear bolt to unthread it behind the boot. [t768]

[Partial] Remove companion flange to access pinion seal, inspect for secondary dust shield or seal behind main. [t119]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Number one, spray PB Blaster onto the bolts frequently over a couple of days.
2. Jack up the truck at your preferred jack point using the h-frame rails in front.
3. Remove both sway bar endlinks from the lower control arm brackets.
4. [Partial] Place a c-clamp under the working side's LCA mount and clamp it inward toward the center of the truck to relieve pressure.
5. Undo the 19mm nut on the stock LCA chassis mount bolts using a breaker bar if necessary.
6. Hammer the nut side of the bolt with a 3 or 4 pound drilling hammer while leaving the nut on for surface area.
7. Alternatively, line up another grade 8 spare bolt and drive it through to break out the stuck one.
8. If needed, use an air hammer to strike the bolt until it frees from its metal sleeve.
9. Immediately replace any removed LCA bolts with adjustable camber bolts oriented so the nut faces forward.
10. Adjust the eccentric washers on the new bolts by playing with the LCA until they catch in the raised edges of the mount.
11. Coat the reinstalled bolt threads generously with anti-seize compound before tightening them down.
12. [Partial] Reinstall both sway bar endlinks and put the tires back onto the wheels.
13. [Partial] Drive to a shop for an alignment, then proceed if you chose Plan A or B instead:
14. [Partial] Apply flame from a torch directly to the bolt's integrated washer side until it gets hot enough to soften the metal.
15. Wiggle the heated bolt out of its sleeve with a socket wrench and hammer it free with your ball peen hammer.
16. Undo the upper control arm spindle attachment using needle nose pliers, a ball peen hammer, and a 22mm socket.
17. Pull the centering pin straight through the UCA hole by gripping its wider loop with the pliers and striking them with the hammer.
18. Support the LCA lightly with a jack while taping back any brake lines to prevent cutting them in half.
19. Grind away material from the side of the seized bolt on the LCA using an angle grinder or sawzall.

_Procedure reported by [t856]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-siezed-cam-bolt-and-lca-removal-and-reinstallation.1214/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t270] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Get a 1-1/2 inch diameter hole saw with a length of 1-3/4 inches.
2. Wear safety goggles and gloves to protect against hot melted rubber.
3. Drill out the center of each stock bushing using a corded, air, or battery-powered drill until two fully charged batteries are depleted.
4. Saw through the outer metal sleeve carefully without cutting into the upper control arm.
5. [Partial] Poke at the edge of the remaining bushing with a hammer and chisel to loosen it for removal.
6. [Partial] Apply copper anti-seize lubricant generously to each new Delrin bushing.
7. Push or knock the first bushing into place using your hands or a block of wood if needed.
8. Assemble the second arm following the same method as the first.
9. Assemble the third arm following the same method as the previous ones.
10. [Partial] Assemble the fourth and final arm to complete the installation.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t811] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Clean the spindle with a stiff wire brush using quick back-and-forth vibrating motions.
2. Avoid brushing smooth mating surfaces designed to fit snugly against the wheel bearing hub assembly too aggressively.
3. Soak critical rusted areas with gelled or liquid rust remover, then rinse thoroughly in lukewarm water and dry completely.
4. Apply a generous amount of WD-40 fish oil-based lubricant to exposed metal surfaces.
5. Rub hard with a stiff nylon dishwashing brush to work the lubricant into the surface.
6. [Partial] Sand down hardened rust accumulation using emery cloth or fine wet/dry sandpaper (P400 grit recommended).
7. If using water for sanding, ensure the spindle is dried thoroughly afterward.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t642] [Partial]</summary>

1. Check Parts Souq to see if they have the bolts in stock.
2. [Partial] Buy four Febest Camber Bolts with part number 0229-004 for $6.95 each.
3. Purchase four Nissan Camber Washers with part number 545591Z600 for $6.15 total.
4. Locate the existing nut from your stock LCA bolts to reuse it free of charge.
5. Install the new hardware on the vehicle's lower control arms.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t768] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the front UCA bolt.
2. Pull the rear UCA bolt out as far as possible from its hole.
3. Twist the entire UCA by pushing the front end inward to angle the rear bolt backward.
4. Unthread the angled rear bolt using channel locks so it passes behind the boot.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t856] [Partial]</summary>

1. Undo the bottom bolt on the spindle that compresses the knuckle around the ball joint end.
2. [Partial] Loosen and remove the nut from this bottom bolt.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t754] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the CV axle from the differential.
2. Use a seal puller with two internal jaws to grip the old side seal inside the housing.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t119] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the companion flange to access the pinion seal.
2. [Partial] Inspect for a secondary dust shield or seal behind the main pinion seal, noting it may be absent despite FSM diagrams.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a quick vibrating motion like an ordinary toothbrush for the wire brushing step. [t811]
- Be gentle with mating surfaces to prevent losing snug fit against the wheel bearing hub assembly. [t811]
- [Partial] Since both sides' sway bars are off, use a jack under the working side's LCA mount to relieve pressure before clamping. [t856]
- Clamp the LCA inwards toward the center of the truck using a big C-clamp. [t856]
- Leave the nut on for a few turns to provide more surface area when pounding. [t856]
- Coat the reinstalled adjustable bolt heavily with anti-seize before inserting it. [t856]
- Straighten one side of the pin before grabbing it with pliers to ensure a clean pull-through. [t856]
- [Partial] Support the LCA and tape back brake lines to prevent cutting them during grinding. [t856]
- [Partial] Use a cheater pipe if extra leverage is needed to break them free initially. [t856]
- [Partial] Use a 19mm socket for the bottom bolt, though confirmation of size may be needed. [t856]
- [Partial] Drive the bolt out using a hammer (BFH) and some random grade eight bolts with PB Blaster to spread it. [t856]
- [Partial] Avoid using a closed-end box wrench or flat screwdriver, as these may push the seal's exterior walls harder into the opening. [t754]
- Reuse the existing nut from stock LCA bolts to save money. [t642]
- [Partial] Look for bolts with degree adjustment markings similar to the OEM style. [t642]
- [Partial] Ensure the bolt is an exact match for alignment shop compatibility. [t642]
- Use the longer version of the 1-1/2 inch hole saw for better depth. [t270]
- Expect to use multiple fully charged batteries if using cordless drills due to heat generation. [t270]
- Wear eye protection and gloves as melted rubber can fly off during drilling. [t270]
- [Partial] Use synthetic grease on the bushing sleeves and outside of the bushes. [t270]
- Apply antiseize only to the outside of the bolts if you want them to slide easily in the sleeves. [t270]
- [Partial] Use an angle grinder to cut the bolt only if space is tight. [t768]
- Ensure the rear bolt angles backward enough to clear the boot. [t768]
- Expect inconsistent diagrams regarding the seal picture. [t119]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Brushing smooth parts too hard and damaging them, [t811]
- Installing the LCA ball joint bolt facing backward instead of forward through the knuckle hole. [t856]
- [Partial] Using too many jawed pullers (like three internal jaws) which failed to budge the seal. [t754]
- [Partial] Pushing the seal inward with a closed-end wrench instead of pulling it straight out. [t754]
- [Partial] Cutting through the UCA while sawing the outer metal sleeve (use caution). [t270]
- [Partial] Failing to use anti-seize which made installation difficult for this user. [t270]
- Not accounting for heat generated by the drill and rubber friction. [t270]
- Using antiseize directly on the outside of the Delrin bushings, as it contains abrasives that can wear down the material. [t270]
- [Partial] Forgetting to grease the bushes which leads to noise after initial break-in. [t270]
- Trying to remove the front bolt before pulling the rear one out first. [t768]
